name: Customer inbox triage and reply drafter
why: Ranks a morning's enquiries and drafts a checked reply for each, the daily start of the enquiry-to-booking workflow.

name: Plan an event follow up that earns a reply
why: Plans a follow-up after a tour, fair or event that gives the buyer a reason to answer, like the hold and quote follow-ups here.

name: Follow-up email sequence writer
why: Turns one message into follow-ups with a new reason each time and a stop rule, the same rule this kit uses for quiet quotes.

name: Offer useful information first and follow up with stalled leads
why: A longer play for leads that stall after the first reply, built on giving something useful before asking again.

name: Turn a sales call into a checked proposal
why: Turns call notes into a proposal with every claim checked and a plan to signature, a companion to the quote and proposal builder.

name: Prepare your first freelance project quote
why: A step-by-step quote for a creative or freelance project, useful for studios setting up their first rate card and quote layout.

name: Explain service booking terms to customers
why: Turns approved booking terms into plain words for buyers, matching the kit's rule to summarise terms without interpreting them.

name: Prepare a hotel group booking handover
why: A ready handover for a confirmed hotel group booking, the venue version of the order and booking handoff skill.

name: Handover note writer
why: Turns a brain dump into a handover note that shows what is due and what breaks first, useful when a coordinator is away.

name: Weekly sales pipeline reviewer
why: Reviews a deal export each week for what changed and what to act on, a reporting partner to the CRM hygiene sweep.

name: Complaint reply promise checker
why: Checks a reply to an upset buyer for promises the business cannot keep, before the owner sends it.

name: Post-sale follow-up planner
why: Plans the thank-you, check-ins and review request after delivery, the step after the handoff closes.

name: Agent action approval builder
why: Plans how an agent asks a person to approve an action, the pattern behind the fresh yes for binding quotes and merges.
